Top Headline Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ) reported better-than-expected earnings and sales for its first quarter, but issued weak Q2 guidance on Thursday. Voices From The Street Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan said Apple’s weak iPhone unit sales were offset by higher-than-expected margins and tax benefits. “In our opinion, the unit growth was indisputably weaker (and our estimates for unit growth have come down although ASPs remain robust) but the stock has a backstop from the company’s ability to opportunistically buy back stock equivalent to 20% of the market capitalization,” Mohan. Management previously issued guidance for revenue between $84 billion and $87 billion for this quarter. AAPL_2018q3.summary_analysis: Coverage portrayed the quarter as broadly stronger than expected: both earnings and sales beat expectations. The coverage also emphasized management's outlook, but did not characterize it consistently as a clear positive or negative. Beyond the headline result, the articles supplied the following operating and market context: Furthermore, AAPL raised guidance for the current quarter to between $60 billion and $62 billion, slightly above Wall Street’s consensus estimate. Solid Guidance Rosenblatt Securities analyst Jun Zhang said Apple’s guidance was better than feared. “We believe Apple will ramp up production of the new LCD iPhone model earlier than expected, and production volume will be larger than the market expects for the September quarter,” Zhang wrote. Longbow Research analyst Shawn Harrison said a richer iPhone mix and an aggressive buyback strategy were two key themes in the quarter. “FY3Q results and F4Q guidance, which was above consensus, highlighted services growth momentum that shows few signs of abating, surprising sustainability of a richer iPhone mix, and the power of AAPL’s balance sheet and decision to accelerate its capital return,” Harrison wrote. Cirrus Logic, Inc. (NASDAQ: CRUS ): Apple's report bodes well for Cirrus Logic's outlook, but limited content gains in the new iPhone imply minimal catalysts ahead for the stock. Buybacks Making An Impact Deutsche Bank analyst Sherri Scribner said iPhone unit growth of just 1 percent was a bit disappointing. “EPS beat expectations by $0.18, but we estimate that just $0.04 of the beat came from revenue upside, while the remaining $0.14 was helped by below-the-line items like higher other income, a lower tax rate and buybacks,” Scribner wrote in a note. Post-release analyst coverage leaned constructive, with more upgrades or target increases than negative revisions. Firms represented included Citigroup, Canaccord Genuity, BMO Capital, Deutsche Bank.
AAPL_2018q3.why_moved: The stock rose 5.7% over the two-day earnings window. The coverage therefore implies that the earnings performance was the first-order positive driver.
